Methods

Reproducible, thresholded evidence monitoring

The site is designed to answer what changed, how strong the evidence is, what the numbers show, how practice may be affected, and what questions will come next.

Site specification

Final name
AD Biomarker Field Brief
One-sentence description
A curated evidence monitor for Alzheimer disease biomarkers, clinical trials, clinical guidelines, and management updates that may change scientific exchange, diagnosis, treatment, care, or access.
Information architecture
Latest, Archive, Landscape, Meeting prep, Methods, About, and RSS; historical coverage is linked from Methods and Archive.
Visual system
Scientific-publication typography, cool neutral surfaces, dark teal accent, text-labeled evidence states, 1100-pixel maximum width, and system light/dark modes.

Inclusion threshold

Biomarker and PET work is the core mission. Core priority includes blood and CSF biomarkers; amyloid, tau, and relevant FDG PET; analytical validity and preanalytics; assay and platform comparisons; cutoffs, gray zones, predictive values, prevalence and comorbidity effects; PET acquisition, visual reading, quantification, Centiloid/SUVR methods, tracer comparability, structured reporting, and reader reproducibility; blood-CSF-PET concordance; sequential testing workflows; treatment eligibility and monitoring; implementation; authorization; coverage; and diagnostic guidance. High-value technical reviews, practice parameters, consensus-to-practice papers, and negative studies can qualify when they materially change interpretation or implementation.

Reviews ordinarily publish zero to five items. Core biomarker/PET items are never omitted because a general-management item filled a quota. If more than five qualify, core items publish first and verified secondary-context items carry forward. General Alzheimer management remains in scope only when it is practice-changing, changes a formal recommendation or access pathway, reports a pivotal or clearly decision-relevant trial, or resolves a major field question. Routine associations, small feasibility pilots, and low-impact management reports are excluded.

Evidence model

Primary sources control. Analytical validity, clinical validity, clinical utility, regulatory authorization, availability, guideline endorsement, and payer coverage are separate fields. Diagnostic results include the actual denominator, reference standard, thresholds, indeterminate range, predictive values, and confidence intervals when the source reports them. Treatment studies report population, design, absolute benefit and harm, follow-up, denominator, and uncertainty when available, and distinguish primary from secondary or exploratory findings. Guidelines identify issuing body, population, recommendation, evidence basis, strength when available, and formal guideline versus consensus status. Guideline recommendations and regulatory details are not invented study results. Cross-study performance is never presented as a head-to-head comparison.

Topic classification

Biomarkers is limited to reports whose central question or primary analysis concerns biomarker measurement, validity, interpretation, implementation, authorization, or coverage. A treatment trial is not classified as biomarker research merely because it measures biomarkers. Clinical Trials identifies primary reports of prospective interventional human trials; Registry Results identifies the rare useful result available only in a public trial registry. It is not an enrollment feed. Evidence syntheses, observational cohorts, regulatory summaries, and guidelines are not trial reports. Topics overlap only when each independently reflects a central purpose of the report.

Structured entry schema

Every entry is stored as validated JSON and includes stable ID/slug, source and added dates, evidence and relevance labels, topic/modality/biomarker/use tags, design or evidence basis, quantitative results or recommendations, interpretation, questions and answers, limitations, platform relevance when applicable, access relevance, source, citation, and correction history. General management entries may leave inapplicable assay fields empty. The same data generate cards, permalinks, archive filters, sitemap, and RSS.

Historical backfill

The original biomarker backfill covered January 1 through September 4, 2026 with a completed month-by-month source-category audit. The September 7 scope expansion adds a separately recorded, targeted 2026 backfill for guidelines and management; it does not extend that original completion claim to all AD care. A focused October 14 criteria audit added four missed biomarker/PET implementation papers and strengthened future source coverage. Historical additions are labeled by their actual source dates, deduplicated against existing entries, and excluded from prospective per-review counts. Zero-result months remain visible. Inspect the coverage audit.

Prospective review

An every-other-day scheduled review begins after launch, with a manual-run option. Discovery queries search all registry categories. The process may publish zero entries. The reviewed-through date advances only after successful screening, primary-source verification, validation, and deployment; an overdue or failed run must not masquerade as current.

Validation and deployment

Before deployment, the build checks required fields, ISO dates, relevance tags, duplicate stable identifiers and slugs, HTTPS primary sources, nonempty findings appropriate to the evidence type, landscape verification dates, and coverage-audit consistency. CSS, JavaScript, entry data, and status data receive content hashes. The deployment package, RSS, sitemap, archive, cards, and landscape are generated in one build.

Corrections

Substantive corrections are appended as dated notes. They are not silently overwritten. To request a correction, provide the stable entry URL, the sentence at issue, and a primary source supporting the change.

Review log

October 26, 2026

Successful review · 1 qualified

All 21 source categories were checked. The carried-forward COGNITE phase III report qualified: ALZT-OP1 failed both prespecified CDR-SB comparisons, and the exploratory APOE4-noncarrier comparison with placebo was not statistically significant. No additional qualifying biomarker/PET, guideline, registry-only, regulatory, authorization, coverage, access, or practice-changing management development was found.

October 24, 2026

Successful review · 5 qualified

All 21 source categories were checked. Five prospective core items qualified, including four October 22 publications newly indexed after the prior review: ABN/RCPsych blood-test guidance, delayed-processing stability of the Lumipulse p-tau217/Aβ42 ratio, a negative SynVesT-1 versus FDG PET head-to-head study, AA-2024 CSF reclassification, and brain-derived tau enrichment for ALS confounding. A verified negative ALZT-OP1 phase III report (DOI:10.1177/13872877261498247; NCT02547818) was carried forward because core evidence filled the five-item cycle. No additional qualifying registry-only, regulatory, coverage, or access development was found.

October 22, 2026

Successful review · 3 qualified

All 21 source categories were checked. Three prospective core items qualified: direction-specific plasma p-tau217/amyloid-PET discordance, automated p-tau217 dual thresholds in a Taiwanese memory clinic, and a diagnostic-accuracy meta-analysis of CSF ratios against amyloid PET. No additional qualifying guideline, trial, registry-only, regulatory, coverage, access or secondary-management development was found.

Source registry

PubMed

Literature · Every review · Last checked October 26, 2026 (Biomarkers, guidelines, and management) · Targeted management check September 7, 2026

Date-bounded searches with a dedicated core pass for blood and CSF biomarkers; amyloid, tau and FDG PET; p-tau species; Aβ42/40; GFAP and NfL; assay comparison, preanalytics, cutoffs, gray zones, prevalence and comorbidity effects; Centiloid/SUVR, tracer comparability, visual reads, structured reporting, concordance, discordance, reflex workflows, treatment eligibility and monitoring. A separate secondary pass covers pivotal treatment, safety, guidance and practice-changing management evidence. Screen reviews and practice standards as well as original studies; deduplicate by PMID and DOI.

Crossref

Literature · Every review · Last checked October 26, 2026 (Biomarkers, guidelines, and management)

First-online date and DOI verification; early-view/final-version deduplication.

Neurology and dementia journals

Literature · Every review · Last checked October 26, 2026 (Biomarkers, guidelines, and management) · Targeted management check September 7, 2026

Current/early-view searches across Alzheimer’s & Dementia, JAMA family, Lancet family, Nature family, Brain, Neurology, geriatric and psychiatric care journals. Include general AD trials, guidelines, safety and management outcomes independently of biomarker implications.

Laboratory medicine and diagnostics journals

Literature · Every review · Last checked October 26, 2026 (Biomarkers, guidelines, and management)

Analytical validation, precision, interference, specimen matrix, tube and processing effects, freeze-thaw stability, standardization, platform transferability, head-to-head assay studies, two-cutoff workflows, predictive values, comorbidity effects, and laboratory implementation searches across Clinical Chemistry, JALM and related diagnostics journals.

Dedicated searches across Journal of Nuclear Medicine, Journal of Nuclear Medicine Technology, European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging, Seminars in Nuclear Medicine, Radiology, and Clinical Nuclear Medicine for amyloid, tau and relevant FDG PET; radiotracers; acquisition and quality control; visual reads and reader agreement; structured reporting; Centiloid/SUVR and reference regions; tracer harmonization; treatment eligibility and monitoring; practice parameters, procedure standards, appropriate-use criteria, and implementation reviews.

Professional guidelines and consensus

Guidelines · Every review · Last checked October 26, 2026 (Biomarkers, guidelines, and management) · Targeted management check September 7, 2026

Alzheimer’s Association, AAN, SNMMI, EANM, ACR, ACNM, ASNR, ADLM, CAP, EAN, WHO, NICE and relevant geriatric/psychiatric societies. Give priority to blood/CSF biomarker guidance, amyloid/tau/FDG PET appropriate-use criteria, procedure standards, acquisition/reading/reporting guidance, diagnosis, staging, treatment eligibility and monitoring. Also screen practice-changing safety, symptoms, caregiver and supportive-care guidance. Distinguish formal CPGs, practice parameters, procedure standards, AURs, consensus and draft versus final guidance.

ClinicalTrials.gov

Clinical trials · Every review · Last checked October 26, 2026 (Biomarkers, guidelines, and management) · Targeted management check September 7, 2026

New and updated AD trials of disease-modifying and symptomatic treatments, nonpharmacologic and caregiver interventions, and biomarker eligibility/endpoints; link results to definitive publications and stable trial identifiers. Registry-only results and enrollment notices are exceptional inclusions and require material field, practice, access, or trial-design relevance plus enough public detail for a useful brief.
